rule.description: The rule deciding whether a record loaded from pyWhat's shipped JSON databases (a regex entry or a file-signature record) is complete enough to be handed into the identification pipeline is a single responsibility of the data access layer; when several pipeline modules each define their own re-statement of that rule, any conceptual change to it requires coordinated edits at every definition site and the copies can silently disagree.

checks.description: Detects a definition named '*entry_ok' whose own body names at least two schema fields of the shipped databases (re-stating the record-completeness rule itself) and that is re-defined independently by at least one other module of the package, i.e. the database-entry trust policy is split across pipeline modules.
checks.detected_relation: pipeline module -> re-implemented database-entry trust policy (independent implementation of a shared admission rule)
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: One conceptual decision - which fields a shipped database record must carry before the pipeline may trust it - is owned by several independent implementations in separate modules. A change to the decision now requires small coordinated edits at every definition site, and the separate copies can silently disagree about the required fields.

matches.evidence: Module-level helper re-states regex-entry completeness as a membership loop over ('Name', 'Rarity', 'Tags'); applied inside Distribution._filter before an entry can enter the distribution pool ('_entry_ok(regex) and regex in self').

Method on the match stage re-states regex-entry completeness over ('Name', 'Description') plus a re-stated sub-record rule for the optional Children block ('method', 'Items'); used as a loop guard at the top of RegexIdentifier.check so entries that fail it never enter match-record construction.

Method on the output layer re-states pattern-record completeness over ('Name', 'Description', 'Tags'); consulted at two render-path call sites (the raw text loop in Printing.print_raw and the format-string substitution loop in Printing.format_print) to drop rows before they are rendered.

Module-level helper re-states file-signature completeness as presence of ('Description', 'ISO 8859-1'); conjoined into the result-assembly condition in Identifier.identify ('if magic_numbers and _signature_entry_ok(magic_numbers)') so a detected signature that fails it is left out of the report.

Second independent re-statement of file-signature completeness, requiring a different field set ('Hexadecimal File Signature', 'Description') than the assembly-side copy; used as a skip guard inside the check_magic_nums scan loop before the signature is dereferenced.

excluded: pywhat/filter.py Filter.__contains__ - applies the user-facing rarity/tag matching window to entries that are already being consumed; it decides which valid entries match a Distribution, not whether a shipped record is complete, and predates the injection (excluded from the rule).

pywhat/helper.py load_regexes() - the loader's existing Children wiring dereferences children['path'] and children['Items'] inside a try/except KeyError; it is the consolidation target the rule points at, not a re-statement, and is not reported.

pywhat/regex_identifier.py RegexIdentifier.check() children matching block - pre-existing dereference of the Children configuration ('children["method"]', 'children["Items"]') with KeyError handling inside the match loop; it consumes an already-admitted entry rather than deciding admission, and is not reported.

pywhat/helper.py AvailableTags / pywhat/printer.py container-shape membership tests - membership tests over report keys or tag sets, not database-record completeness; similar in shape but intentionally outside the rule.

definitions that re-state the rule under a name outside the '*entry_ok' family are anchored by name and therefore not reported by this rule; that residual is covered instance-side by the solver rubrics rather than by the structural rule.
